Nyirkata Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Császári utca 33, Hungary

Not demolished. Nyírkáta's Jewish community, first settled at the end of the 18th century, joined the Orthodox stream following the 1869 schism at the Jewish Congress that divided Hungarian Jewry between Orthodox and Maskilim factions; it maintained a burial society and a synagogue built in 1840. Following the German occupation in 1944, immediately after Passover, the community was sent to the Mátészalka Ghetto and deported to Auschwitz in early June; no Jewish community remained afterward. This cemetery, established as early as 1858, was originally divided into two sections, since merged under a single fence.
